subject: Onboarding: model shortlist + initial token / context sizing for Quantile Health
messages:
From: Erin Cole <erin.cole@quantilehealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: model / sizing guidance after demo

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the demo this morning. A few follow-ups from our side as we prep the internal buy-in:

- Quick context: Quantile Health plans to ship an assistant for clinician chart summarization + short Q&A. Expected pilot: ~3,000 unique clinicians (pilot cohort) over 2 months; estimated concurrent active users ~120 during clinic hours.
- Current queries: average prompt length ~180 tokens, expected average generated summary ~700 tokens. Some workflows (discharge summaries) may need longer context up to ~16k tokens, but that will be <5% of calls.
- Our priorities: predictable latency during office hours, reasonable unit cost, and a clear plan for evaluating quality regressions across models.

Can you/your team provide: 1) a short model shortlist for pilot + rationale, 2) suggested default context length for pilot (8k vs 32k tradeoffs), and 3) a back-of-envelope monthly token estimate for the pilot? We'll surface that to procurement.

I've attached an anonymized week of sample events (small CSV) so you can sanity-check assumptions.

Thanks — happy to hop on another 30-min sync if useful.

—Erin
Quantile Health

[Attachment: quantile_usage_sample.csv (csv, 48KB)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Erin Cole <erin.cole@quantilehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model / sizing guidance after demo

Erin — thanks for the sample and the context; very helpful. High-level recommendations for the pilot below (assumptions listed at the end). If this looks good, Monica will take the lead on the implementation plan and Ben will scope the capacity/costs.

Model shortlist (pilot tier -> fallback):
1) redwood-instruct-13b-quant (recommended) — good balance of latency and instruction-following for summarization tasks; quantized profile keeps cost predictable.
2) mistral-instruct-7b (alternative) — slightly cheaper on tokens, competitive quality on short summaries; useful for lower-cost A/B.
3) llm-70b-q4f (high-quality fallback) — for the <5% long-context discharge summaries where quality matters more than cost. We recommend routing those to an isolated longer-context variant to avoid impacting SLOs.

Context length / tradeoffs:
- Default pilot context: 8k tokens. Rationale: covers ~95% of your weekly interactions (based on the sample), keeps GPU memory and latency predictable, and reduces per-request cost.
- Long-context path: 32k-enabled variant for specific discharge-summary flows (will be used ~5% of calls in your profile). Route these to a separate pool with autoscaling and an explicit SLA.

Back-of-envelope token estimate (pilot, month 1):
- Pilot cohort: 3,000 clinicians (active subset ~1,800 monthly).
- Avg queries/day per clinician (clinic days): 4 -> ~7,200 requests/day.
- Avg prompt tokens: 200; avg response tokens: 700 -> 900 tokens/request total (prompt + response + overhead).
- Monthly requests: 7,200 * 22 clinic days ≈ 158,400 requests/month.
- Monthly tokens ≈ 158,400 * 900 ≈ 142,560,000 tokens (~143M).
- Long-context 32k calls (5%): 7,920 requests/month * avg 10k tokens ≈ 79.2M tokens; these are currently included in the 143M estimate if rerouted we treat separately.

Operational notes / next steps:
- We'll run a 7-day load test on Dedicated capacity to validate latency and cost curves before pilot launch.
- Monica: please confirm timing for sample ingestion and initial eval runs.
- Ben: can you draft an estimated monthly bill for 8k default vs 32k-hybrid route (include burst + canary)?

Attached a quick spreadsheet with the calculations. If everything looks good, we'll prepare a mutual action plan and a 30-min tech kickoff next week.

—Lauren Bishop
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: initial_token_model_estimates.xlsx (xlsx, 22KB)]

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model / sizing guidance after demo

Thanks Lauren — I'm looping in operations and I can own the implementation runbook. Quick notes: 

- I'll need the sample CSV mounted to our secure test bucket (please confirm S3 or GDrive).
- Plan: run a two-step validation: 1) correctness eval on a 1k-sample subset across the three model candidates; 2) 7-day throughput test at peak clinic-hour QPS to validate latency SLOs.
- For throughput testing, recommend Dedicated pool with the following starting config: 4x A100s, continuous batching enabled, KV prefix caching set for patient-context reuse. We'll scale after the first 48 hours based on tail latencies.

Action items assigned to me:
- Prepare eval harness and metrics dashboard (quality/regression hooks).
- Coordinate with Ben on resource provisioning and HubSpot playbook.
- Draft a simple canary rollout for the 32k path (route ~2% traffic initially).

I'll follow up by Monday with a proposed test calendar.

—Monica
Customer Success Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model / sizing guidance after demo

Sounds good — two quick questions:
1) Do we want the canary for 32k enabled as a config on the pilot from day 1, or start strictly with 8k and open 32k after validation? My recommendation: start 8k default with 32k canary at 1-2% so we can capture quality deltas without blowing cost.
2) I'll create an A/B route in the console for redwood-instruct-13b-quant vs mistral-instruct-7b for cost/quality comparison; add HS link to the deal notes.

Link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/98721

—Ben
